history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - keep-or-drop decision needed. The Ratan Bai Masjid is a Dawoodi Bohra mosque in Jamnagar, built in the late 19th century by Ratan Bai - described by one source as a Bohra businesswoman and by another as the wife of a local Bohra community leader (minor conflict; the name is the same). Built during the reign of the Jam Sahebs of Nawanagar, it is made of yellow sandstone with a large central dome, minarets and stained-glass windows, blending Islamic and European architectural styles reflecting Bohra cosmopolitanism. It serves as both a place of worship and a Bohra community centre. Address: Ranjit Road / Panchasar, Kadiawad, Jamnagar.

name: Ratan Bai Masjid
town_description: Jamnagar is a historic port and industrial city in Saurashtra, founded as Nawanagar by the Jadeja Rajputs in the 16th century. It is known for the Lakhota Lake and Palace, Bala Hanuman Temple, and as one of Gujarat's major trade and refining centres.
